AC5: "`messageLineSchema` carries an upper bound on `seq`, a line above that bound is refused at read, and `nextSeq` refuses to build on an out-of-range recorded value; a test that appends a crafted line fails if the room is unwritable afterwards." -> "`messageLineSchema` bounds `seq` on the WRITE path so roomyx itself cannot produce an out-of-range line, reading stays permissive so a hand-crafted line cannot make an existing log unreadable, and `nextSeq` ignores an out-of-range recorded value when allocating rather than building on it; a test that appends a crafted line at the safe-integer ceiling fails if the room is unwritable afterwards, and a companion test fails if that line stops the log being read." (As frozen, AC5 required a line above the bound to be 'refused at read'. The T5 author showed that turns an unwritable room into an unreadable one — the worse failure for an append-only log with no repair command, and the exact class D-08 exists to prevent. The criterion described a fix that trades a recoverable fault for an unrecoverable one. Corrected to bound the write path and keep reads tolerant. No confirmations existed to void.)
